messages:
miriam (oncall): paging: p95/p99 spike for /streaming/generate in us-west-2, alerting SLOs breached :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-4182 opened (severity: high) — seen p95 420ms -> 1.2s, p99 1.6s -> 3.4s, increased streaming stalls.
ellie (support): several customer sessions reported stalls and stalled tokens, some reconnect loops. I can share example session ids privately.
raj (SRE): seeing correlated KV cache eviction rate up 8x over baseline since 11:03 UTC, prefill bytes per second spiking vs decode throughput — looks like prefill is thrashing slabs.
lucas (infra): confirmed. kv-cache slab allocation graph shows repeated shrink/expand cycles. fragmentation metric (kv.slab.frag_ratio) jumped from 0.12 -> 0.61.
amanda (runtime): that frag ratio will cause many cache misses + re-prefill work during streaming which inflates tail. prefill vs decode imbalance: prefills are dominating, decoder threads are starved.
raj (SRE): quick mitigation proposals: 1) increase slab target to avoid shrink churn (hot path) 2) throttle prefill rate briefly 3) route streaming to fallback small-quant model for heavy tail customers 4) temporarily disable long-tail streaming for non-SLA customers.
elliE (support): (typo) ellie: +1 on routing heavy customers off while we mitigate. Which customers are impacted?
ellie (support): impacted customers: acme-data, snaplogic, and two trial orgs — first outreach in progress.
sara (product): notify reps for acme-data + include ETA and compensatory credits if >30m.
miriam (oncall): executing mitigation step 1: bumping kv slab soft_limit from 256MB -> 640MB on prod-kv-pool-usw2 to reduce shrink thrash. Doing rolling config update now.
lucas (infra): command I'm running (kubectl ctx prod-usw2):
```
kubectl -n inference set env ds/kv-cache KV_SLAB_SOFT_LIMIT=640MB
kubectl rollout restart ds/kv-cache
```
lucas (infra): rolling restarts started, expecting pods to come back in ~40s each, monitoring.
amanda (runtime): applying a short-term prefill throttle too: setting PREFILL_RATE_LIMIT=0.5 (50% of normal) for streaming route.
raj (SRE): while restarts progress, enabling route fallback for top noisy orgs: update router rule to map org ids -> model-variant: small-quant.
raj (SRE): router change (preview):
```
route /streaming/generate {
  if org in ["acme-data","snaplogic"] then model = "rw-sm-q2"
}
```
miriam (oncall): customer impact check: p95 dropped to 280ms after first pod replaced, p99 trending down but still 1.1s. streaming stall count down 60% on affected nodes.
ellie (support): acme-data acknowledged degrade, they see improvement after switchover. keeping them patched.
amanda (runtime): root cause summary hypothesis: KV slab shrink policy + high bursty prefill patterns cause fragmentation; reclamation leads to extra work on prefill hot keys and decode backpressure => streaming stalls and long tail.
sara (product): can we capture deterministic repro? we need a playback of a high-concurrency prefill burst to test slab behavior.
raj (SRE): will create a loadtest in staging that hits prefill-heavy workload with small keys to reproduce fragmentation. tagging this as follow-up: KV-5479.
lucas (infra): long term mitigation ideas: 1) adjust slab compaction heuristics 2) per-org prefill quotas 3) separate slab pools for streaming vs batch 4) allocate headroom in soft_limit by default.
amanda (runtime): patch ready for per-tenant prefill throttle feature — needs canary and perf run, target ship in 2 sprints.
miriam (oncall): operational action items before handoff:
- keep PREFILL_RATE_LIMIT=0.5 for 20m then re-evaluate
- keep acme-data/snaplogic routed to small-quant until p99 < 800ms for 30m
- watch kv.slab.frag_ratio, kv.evictions.rate, streaming.stalls and p99/p95
- notify ops if any pod fail >2 restarts in 10m

Handoff: I'm handing off to raj (SRE) for overnight monitoring at 01:00 UTC. Current status: slab bump applied, prefill throttle active, router fallback in place.
raj (SRE): acknowledged. I'll keep alerts tuned to p99>900ms and paging thresholds. If stalls reappear we'll revert PREFILL_RATE_LIMIT -> 0.8 and scale Dedicated pool by +2 nodes.
sara (product): thanks team — I'll coordinate comms and customer notes.
miriam (oncall): final note for runbook: add KV frag playbook link: https://confluence.redwood/kb/kv-frag-playbook (see steps for slab bump & rollback).
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-4182 updated: mitigations applied. Next update planned in 30m or on significant change.
raj (SRE): leaving a short checklist for overnight:
- monitor p95/p99 and streaming stalls
- watch for new noisy orgs and add routing exceptions
- follow up with engineering on slab compaction ticket KV-5482

miriam (oncall): thanks everyone, handing off.
